factual_errors.claim: 'Reconnect power -- re-apply the nominal supply (typically 24 V DC) while keeping the device isolated from the drive line.'
factual_errors.why_wrong: The AC 01.2 actuator controller is a mains/three-phase-AC powered device, not a 24V DC device. Presenting 24V DC as the 'typical' nominal supply for this controller is factually wrong and could lead a technician to misidentify or mis-test the power system.

factual_errors.claim: 'Launch AUMA's bootloader/firmware tool... connect via the RS-485 or USB port as specified for the AC 01.2' / 'does the bootloader utility detect the controller... when you start the scan?'
factual_errors.why_wrong: Documented AC 01.2 firmware recovery is via Bluetooth (AUMA CDT app) or SD card at a restricted service level -- there is no USB/RS-485 bootloader port or generic 'AUMA Firmware Update' PC tool in the documented recovery path. This invents an entire recovery workflow that doesn't match the real procedure.

factual_errors.claim: 'Select the correct firmware file... start the upload; the tool should detect the bootloader and write the firmware.'
factual_errors.why_wrong: Firmware for this device is model/serial-specific and must be obtained directly from AUMA service, not selected freely by the technician from a generic file. Nothing in the answer flags that this is a restricted, authorization-gated operation.

notes: This answer repeats essentially the same critical defects the 09-05 grading round already flagged and failed for this exact question: wrong power-supply assumption (24V DC vs. the actual AC supply), an invented USB/RS-485 bootloader workflow when the documented recovery is Bluetooth-CDT or SD-card at restricted service level, and a generic 'AUMA Firmware Update' tool that isn't part of the real procedure -- all stated with full confidence and no disclosure that this is unverified general reasoning. For a bricked actuator controller stuck in bootloader mode, following this procedure would very likely fail to recover the device and could risk further damage from applying the wrong recovery path to restricted service-level hardware. The general_reasoning fallback path clearly did not fix the underlying problem that abstention fixed for the same question in the machine_selected condition.
